stimulus.text:
Judith Sargent Murray, “On the Equality of the Sexes,” Massachusetts Magazine, 1790 (written in 1779):

“Is it upon mature consideration we adopt the idea, that nature is thus partial in her distributions? Is it indeed a fact, that she hath yielded to one half of the human species so unquestionable a mental superiority? ... Are we deficient in reason? We can only reason from what we know, and if an opportunity of acquiring knowledge hath been denied us, the inferiority of our sex cannot fairly be deduced from thence.”
stimulus.source_note: Judith Sargent Murray, “On the Equality of the Sexes,” Massachusetts Magazine, 1790. Public domain.

source: original; stimulus quoted verbatim from Judith Sargent Murray, “On the Equality of the Sexes,” Massachusetts Magazine, 1790. Public domain.

primary_sources: Judith Sargent Murray, “On the Equality of the Sexes” (1790)

stem: According to Murray, women’s inferiority cannot fairly be judged because...

options.text: women have never written anything worth reading.
options.misconception: Murray herself wrote this essay, and she argues women were denied the chance to learn.

options.text: men are naturally weaker in reason than women.
options.misconception: Murray claims the minds of the sexes are equal by nature, not that men are weaker.

options.text: women were denied the opportunity to acquire knowledge.
the Massachusetts Magazine refused to print her essay.
options.misconception: The essay appeared in the Massachusetts Magazine in 1790, so it was printed.

rationales.C: Murray says, “We can only reason from what we know, and if an opportunity of acquiring knowledge hath been denied us, the inferiority of our sex cannot fairly be deduced.”
rationales.A: Murray’s own essay disproves the claim that women wrote nothing worth reading.
rationales.B: Murray argues the sexes are equal by nature, not that men are weaker.
rationales.D: The essay was printed in the Massachusetts Magazine in 1790.
rationales.general:
1. Murray says we can only reason from what we know.
2. She then says knowledge was denied to women.
3. From that she concludes their inferiority cannot fairly be judged.
4. Background: Murray wrote the essay in 1779, and it appeared in print in 1790.
5. So the reason is the denied opportunity to acquire knowledge.
Remember: quote the sentence that gives the reason, not the sentence that asks the question.
